description: Composite TEM figure of the boundary κ-carbide in the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel annealed at 1200 °C, containing three panels of three different kinds. (a) is a bright-field (BF) TEM micrograph in which two large α grains are separated by a straight, bright band-like boundary phase labelled κ (orange arrow); dislocation substructure is visible in the lower α grain, and a 200 nm scale bar sits at bottom left. (b) is a selected-area diffraction pattern (SADP) of α and κ: a white-spot diffraction pattern on a black background accompanied by an indexed schematic built on red (α) and yellow (κ) reflections, labelled (-110)α, (110)κ, (11-1)κ and (200)κ, with the zone axis written as z = [001]κ, [001]κ//[011]α and (110)α//(11-1)κ. (c) is a dark-field (DF) micrograph formed with the (200)κ reflection taken from the [110]κ direction; the same boundary appears as discontinuous bright κ segments (arrowed) in a dark α matrix, with a 200 nm scale bar at bottom left. Together the panels argue that the boundary κ is a distinct phase crystallographically related to α by an N–W orientation relationship, yet neighbouring κ particles are largely misoriented, so only part of the boundary lights up in DF.
measured_quantities: diffraction spot positions / zone axis (crystallographic indices, no unit)

observations.observation: In (a) the boundary phase κ appears as a single continuous bright band separating two large α grains, with dark dislocation contrast inside the adjacent α grain.
Both TEM micrographs (a) and (c) carry a 200 nm scale bar in their lower-left corner.
Panel (c) is a dark-field image in which the boundary κ is not continuous but appears as discrete bright segments along the boundary line, while the α matrix is dark.
The indexed schematic beside the (b) diffraction pattern labels reflections (-110)α, (110)κ, (11-1)κ and (200)κ, with α reflections in red and κ reflections in yellow.
The text annotation in (b) states the zone axis condition z = [001]κ, [001]κ//[011]α and (110)α//(11-1)κ.
The caption states that (a) is a BF micrograph, (b) is the SADP of α and κ, and (c) is a (200)κ DF micrograph taken from the [110]κ direction, all for the specimen annealed at 1200 °C.
The citing text states that the SADP in Fig. 12(b) shows the N–W orientation relationship between κ-carbide and α matrix.

The citing text states that the (200) DF micrograph taken from the [110]κ direction shows only part of the boundary κ-carbide, indicating a large misorientation between neighbouring κ-carbide particles.

The citing text states that the boundary κ-carbide is believed to form during quenching when the annealing temperature exceeds the κ-carbide dissolution temperature, which lies between 850 °C and 900 °C.
The citing text places this figure in the series Figs. 10–12 that confirms κ-carbide along α/α boundaries in specimens annealed from 900 °C to 1200 °C.
No numeric measurement (particle size, boundary width, d-spacing) is printed anywhere in the figure; the only printed quantitative element is the 200 nm scale bar.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 1200 °C-annealed specimen showing a bright, straight band of boundary κ (orange arrow) running between two large α grains; dislocation substructure in the lower α grain; 200 nm scale bar at bottom left.

SADP of α and κ: a black-background diffraction spot pattern next to an indexed schematic with red α and yellow κ reflections labelled (-110)α, (110)κ, (11-1)κ, (200)κ; text states z = [001]κ, [001]κ//[011]α, (110)α//(11-1)κ.

Dark-field TEM micrograph taken with the (200)κ reflection from the [110]κ direction; the boundary κ appears as discontinuous chains of bright segments (arrowed) in a dark α matrix; 200 nm scale bar at bottom left.
